correctness.rationale: Complete analytic proof: crown all-set classification yields \(x^4(R_n^2-C_n)\), and \(R_n(0)=C_n>\sqrt{C_n}\). Its Taylor-integral representation makes R_n strictly increasing for odd n and strictly positive/convex for even n. Values at -2,-1 isolate two simple nonzero real crossings. Uniform convergence \(R_n(-y)/n\) to \(1/y\) on \([1,2]\) gives the right root limit; the exact parity-separated exponential identities prove \((\log n+\log c_n+o(1))/n\) for the left-root displacement. Separate exhaustive vertex-subset counts for n=3..8 and illustrative bisections to n=301 agree. Numerical checks are not used to prove infinity.

originality.rationale: The crown connected-domination polynomial and its minimum are prior facts and expressly not claimed as new. The final claim adds exactly two simple nonzero real roots for every n, both strict locations and two different precise limit laws including the odd/even logarithmic constant. Full-text examination of relevant connected-domination papers, graph-root paper and crown-specific article and targeted mathematical database/web queries identified no statement covering these analytic assertions. The prior enumerator determines coefficients but does not state or immediately certify uniform real-root geometry and sharp parity asymptotics. The residual possibility of unindexed equivalent results is acknowledged.
residual_risks: The crown connected-domination polynomial is preexisting; analytic properties are derived from it. No novelty is claimed for that formula or connected domination number.
Unindexed or non-English literature or undocumented computer-algebra tables might already have the two-root statement or parity asymptotics.

Full text of some record-indexed mathematical findings could not be obtained through web access; available claim abstracts were used only to identify possible overlap, not to certify whole-text noncoverage.

value.rationale: Sharp all-order root count, intervals and two distinct asymptotic mechanisms for a natural standard graph family answer a motivated analytic question in current graph-polynomial root research. The even/odd constants in logarithmic-over-linear convergence are structural, not mere recomputation of coefficients or a negligible numerical increment. The result extends available enumeration in a mathematically substantial direction, while conceding the enumerator itself as prior.
